title: Reverend Jenkins and life in the orphanage
summary: He describes the director, the big stone building, and Cat Anderson's report of severe punishments.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, who was the man -- who was the director?
Reverend Jenkins.
It was Reverend Jenkins?
Reverend Jenkins.
He must have been a -- good person.
Yeah, yeah.
It took alot of foresight.
Yeah.
How old would the kids be when they would leave the orphanage -- sixteen I suppose?
Well, yeah. You know, after they get about sixt--
When they get through --
Yeah.
When they could get out of school.
Yeah. When they could get out. You know, they would go.
Fancy that. Do you remember their orphanage where they lived?
Yes.
What did it look like?
A big -- a great big, huge, stone place surrounded by a wall, more or less. It was okay -- but, I never did get too close, you know, to it.
Well, I mean, it would be partly like a reform school?
A reform -- yeah. A regular -- like a regular reform school. The kids couldn't -- they couldn't get out. It's not like they had them fenced in.
No.
I didn't get that impression.
No.
I don't think the kids really wanted to leave, anyway.
Yeah.
Or get away.
Yeah.
I don't think it was like penal, they were like a penal thing, you know.
No.
They seemed like they had alot of freedom, as far as I could tell. The gates and the doors seemed to be open.
Yeah. What do you think Stan?
Seems to me that Cat told me that they had pretty severe punishments and things.
They did?
Yeah.
I don't remember that, because, being on the outside, I don't know what happened on the inside.
They probably didn't need to, either.
I think, you know, he said they'd have to stand on this tree stump for hours, you know, without moving, and things like that, if they did anything wrong.
Oh yeah, how a lot of schools were,
But that was (unintelligible) You know, fifty years ago -- Protestants were much more severe
Yeah, I imagine so.
Yeah.
I don't know. As I say I didn't get that impression, because I was never that close.
No. You were only just following those bands.
Yeah.
